title: Event 1
content:
Summary Report: “The Thinking Behind Building The Bot” Event Objectives Officially kick off FCAJ Buildrathon 2026 (Season 01) Share practical thinking on building AI Agents Connect participants with an industry partner (CMC Global) Speakers Thien Lu – Program Manager, FCAJ Truong Bui – Tech Lead, CMC Global Phong Pham – Program Manager, FCAJ Key Highlights Kickoff of FCAJ Buildrathon 2026 Starting the Buildrathon journey together with everyone Talkshow “The Thinking Behind Building The Bot” with CMC Global Laying a solid architecture foundation for a bot → prioritize less critical tasks first, such as answering repetitive questions or aggregating bugs reported by users Optimizing AI Agents in an enterprise environment: always set up the agent’s soul, skill and rule files so it keeps doing the right job and users cannot exploit its tokens for personal purposes Breaking down the challenges Understanding the current difficulties of the industry, job opportunities, and future career directions Key Takeaways The learning approach and shared vision of the Buildrathon The mindset for setting up AI Agents: optimizing repetitive steps or steps with many unnecessary intermediate stages Applying to Work Optimize AI Agents with different rules and skills for each task (information aggregation, project security checks, …) Event Experience Attending the “The Thinking Behind Building The Bot” talkshow was a very valuable experience, giving me a comprehensive view of how to build and optimize AI Agents in practice. Some highlights:
Learning from highly skilled speakers The speakers shared real enterprise cases that have already been deployed to production Through real case studies, I better understood how to apply AI Agents to large projects in a reasonable way Event Photos

title: Event 2
content: Summary Report: “AWS Cloud Day And AI Day Hanoi - Watch party” Event Objectives Watch AWS Cloud & AI Day Hanoi 2026 live (watch party), held in Hanoi on 29/09/2026 Catch up on the latest trends in Agentic AI, data, migration and modern application development on AWS Hear Vietnamese companies share how they use Cloud and AI Speakers H.E. Hoang Minh – Deputy Minister of Science and Technology H.E. Jennifer Wicks – U.S. Ambassador to Vietnam Dr. Werner Vogels – CTO, Amazon.com Eric Yeo – Country General Manager, Malaysia, Vietnam, Indochina, AWS Mai Le – Director of Product Management, Katalon Dr. Jens Lottner – Chief Executive Officer, Techcombank Key Highlights Keynote: “What does it take to solve problems everyone says are impossible?” Opened with speeches from the Ministry of Science and Technology and the U.S. Ambassador about technology cooperation Werner Vogels talked about solving “impossible” problems with Cloud and AI Techcombank and Katalon shared real stories of bringing AI into their companies Sessions after the keynote Building software with agentic AI → using AI agents across the whole software process From Demo to Deployment → the hard parts of taking Agentic AI from demo to production Building an AI-ready data foundation → getting data ready before doing AI Migration at Scale with Agentic AI → using AWS Transform to move old systems to the cloud faster Platform Engineering at Scale → VPBank shared how they built an Internal Developer Platform on EKS Key Takeaways Agentic AI is AWS’s main focus now, not just for chatting but for doing real work (writing code, migration, …) Good AI needs well-prepared data first Big Vietnamese companies (banks, software companies) already run AI in production, not just experiments The many case studies from large-scale projects were very useful (but because the scale was so big, the talks were short and the demos a bit fast, I didn’t fully understand them in depth, just enough to catch a few keywords) Applying to Work Try AI agents to help write code and tests in projects, but still review the results Pay attention to how data is organized from the start so AI is easier to apply later Event Experience An exciting, lively atmosphere both in Hanoi and at the Watch Party Getting to see highly experienced speakers share their perspectives clearly, along with practical case studies Event Photos

title: Event 3
content:
Summary Report: “Fireside Chat with Dr. Werner Vogels” Event Objectives Meet and talk with Dr. Werner Vogels, CTO of Amazon Hear his view on the future of Cloud and AI Learn from Amazon’s experience building and running systems at global scale Speakers Dr. Werner Vogels – Chief Technology Officer & Vice President, Amazon My Nguyen – Sr. Prototyping Architect, AWS Vietnam Key Highlights The story behind Dynamo Amazon once had its system down for a whole day during the shopping season because its relational database was overloaded → millions of dollars lost Looking back, most of the data only needed simple key-value lookups, and very little really needed a relational database So Amazon built its own key-value store, the ancestor of DynamoDB How Amazon runs its systems Don’t look at the average, look at P99.9 to see what the slowest users are going through “Everything fails all the time” → design the system to keep running when a data center fails GameDays: deliberately shut down real data centers to test whether the system can fail over on its own “Renaissance Developer” A developer in the AI era needs to: stay curious and keep learning, think in systems, own the code they ship, go deep in one area while understanding the others, and communicate well with the team and customers AI is just a tool AI makes prototyping much faster, but the code it writes still has to be checked by a human Grace Hopper said: “The most dangerous phrase is: ‘We’ve always done it this way.’” Key Takeaways Choose technology based on what the system really needs, not out of habit Always be prepared for the system to fail Developers are still needed with AI around, as long as they keep learning and take ownership of their work Applying to Work Review and test AI-written code carefully before using it (security, edge cases, …) Look at how the data is actually used before choosing a database for a project Event Experience Hearing Amazon’s CTO speak in person was a really memorable experience. Some highlights:
Real stories from someone who was there Instead of theory, Werner told real incidents and decisions from Amazon, which made it easy to understand why AWS services are designed the way they are The part about developers in the AI era made me worry less and showed me which skills I need to work on Event Photos
